# signup

Anonymous self-signup: an unauthenticated stranger requesting, verifying, and provisionally checking a username for a new tenant before anything durable is minted.

## POST /v1/silos/{silo_id}/signup

Operation `signup_request_create`.

Request a signup for `email`, redeeming an invite `code` when one is supplied and solving the anti-automation challenge in the same call. A silo whose `invite_required` is `false` admits a caller holding no code; read `invite_required` from `signup-config` to know which. A code supplied to such a silo is still validated and redeemed.

**Always answers 202 with the identical [`SignupAccepted`] body**, whether the submission was accepted or refused. The refusals it hides, in full: the code doesn't exist, is revoked, expired, exhausted, or is bound to a different address; no code was presented to a silo that requires one; `tos_version` is not exactly the silo's authoritative ToS version, the one `signup-config` reports; or signup stopped being enabled, on the silo's policy or on the cluster switch, between this request's own check and the write.

See [`SignupRequestCreate`]'s own doc for the full enumeration-resistance argument and `Store::create_signup_request` for how the store already conflates every one of those refusals into one shape. **A failed challenge is the one exception**: it answers 400, because it reveals only that the caller's own submission didn't verify, never anything about `code` or `email`.

The terms mismatch is the refusal an integrator is most likely to hit and least able to see: sending a stale `tos_version`, or none where the policy names one, makes every signup disappear behind a 202. Send back exactly what `signup-config` reported.

Rate-limited per source address prefix, independently of every other bucket on this surface.

| Parameter | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `silo_id` | path | yes | string (uuid) |  |

Request body (required): `application/json`: [SignupRequestCreate](schemas.md#signuprequestcreate)

Responses:

- `202`: successfully enqueued operation, `application/json`: [SignupAccepted](schemas.md#signupaccepted)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)

## GET /v1/silos/{silo_id}/signup/{request_id}/available

Operation `signup_username_probe`.

Username availability -- reachable ONLY from inside a redeemed, still-live session.

The caller must present the session's own credential: `Bearer <session_token>` (from `session_token`) on the `Authorization` header, checked against `Store::get_signup_session`'s stored `token_hash`, constant-time. A missing/wrong bearer, a `request_id` that names no session (never existed, expired, or already consumed by a later `/complete`), and a session that belongs to a different silo all answer with the same 404 -- this is deliberately not an anonymous enumeration surface at all; `SELF_SIGNUP.md` D2 spells out why both legacy portals' unauthenticated availability checks were themselves an enumeration oracle.

| Parameter | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `request_id` | path | yes | string (uuid) |  |
| `silo_id` | path | yes | string (uuid) |  |
| `username` | query | yes | string |  |

Responses:

- `200`: successful operation, `application/json`: [UsernameAvailability](schemas.md#usernameavailability)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)

## POST /v1/silos/{silo_id}/signup/{request_id}/complete

Operation `signup_complete`.

Gated exactly like `signup_username_probe`: the caller must present `Authorization: Bearer <session_token>` for the redeemed [`SignupSessionIssued`] named by `request_id`. A missing/wrong bearer, an unknown session, a session belonging to a different silo, or one already expired or consumed all answer with the same 404 -- see `signup_username_probe`'s own doc.

Rate-limited per source address prefix, in its own bucket --see `rate_limit::signup_complete_limiter`'s own doc for why it is tighter than every bucket but `resend`'s: this is the single most expensive route on the whole anonymous surface.

| `silo_id` | path | yes | string (uuid) |  |

## POST /v1/silos/{silo_id}/signup/{request_id}/resend

Operation `signup_resend`.

Resend the verification mail for a still-pending signup request: mint a new secret, rotate it onto the request, and queue the mail carrying the new link. The link already in the mailbox stops verifying the instant the rotation commits.

**Always answers 202 with the identical [`SignupAccepted`] body**, matching `signup_request_create`'s own conflation and for the same reason: a `request_id` that is real, expired, or never existed must not be distinguishable from one another. A wrong `verification_token` joins that same conflation.

Because rotation destroys a credential someone else may be holding, the caller must prove it holds the current one: the body carries the plaintext verification token, checked constant-time by `Store::rotate_signup_request_token`. Without it, a `request_id` read out of a log or audit record would be enough to kill a stranger's live link and mail their address again.

Rate-limited far tighter than every other bucket on this surface, per source address prefix.

| Parameter | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `request_id` | path | yes | string (uuid) |  |
| `silo_id` | path | yes | string (uuid) |  |

Request body (required): `application/json`: [SignupResendRequest](schemas.md#signupresendrequest)

Responses:

- `202`: successfully enqueued operation, `application/json`: [SignupAccepted](schemas.md#signupaccepted)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)

## POST /v1/silos/{silo_id}/signup/{request_id}/verify

Operation `signup_verify`.

Redeem the token from the emailed verification link, atomically trading the [`SignupRequestCreate`]-created request for a [`SignupSessionIssued`] -- the one response on this whole surface that hands back a usable, single-use credential.

A wrong token, an expired request, and a never-existed or already-redeemed `request_id` all answer with the same 404 --see `Store::redeem_signup_request`'s own doc for why. A request redeems exactly once: a replay of the same token against the same id, after the first redemption cleared the row, is indistinguishable from "never existed".

| Parameter | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `request_id` | path | yes | string (uuid) |  |
| `silo_id` | path | yes | string (uuid) |  |

Request body (required): `application/json`: [SignupVerifyRequest](schemas.md#signupverifyrequest)

Responses:

- `200`: successful operation, `application/json`: [SignupSessionIssued](schemas.md#signupsessionissued)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)

## GET /v1/silos/{silo_id}/signup-config

Operation `signup_config_view`.

Public signup-form configuration: which challenge to solve (with a freshly issued one when it is ALTCHA), the ToS document id, whether an invite code is required, and whether the eventual admission gate requires payment.

This is the only readable source of `invite_required` and `tos_version`. `POST .../signup` refuses both a missing code and a terms version that is not exactly the policy's behind the same 202 it answers everything else with, so a form that does not read them here cannot tell why its submissions vanish.

A nonexistent silo and a silo with signup disabled answer with the identical 404 -- see the module note above. Carries deliberately less than [`SiloSignupPolicy`]; see `system_silo_signup_policy_view`'s own doc for why that record has no silo-member read at all, let alone an anonymous one.

| Parameter | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `silo_id` | path | yes | string (uuid) |  |

Responses:

- `200`: successful operation, `application/json`: [SignupConfig](schemas.md#signupconfig)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
